charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Ventas, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Ventas, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Ventas, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Ventas, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Ventas, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
The share of lettable space (or units) that is leased.

For Ventas, Inc.: occupancy below the sector norm is the first sign of rental pressure.

What to watch:

  • Occupancy trend
  • Lease expiries in the next two years

revPorShop.title: SHOP RevPOR
revPorShop.content:
RevPOR (revenue per occupied room) is average monthly revenue per occupied unit across Ventas's Senior Housing Operating Portfolio (SHOP) -- the directly-operated senior housing communities, about half of consolidated NOI.

For Ventas, Inc.: SHOP same-store NOI growth decomposes into occupancy (rooms filled) times RevPOR (price per room); rising RevPOR with flat or rising occupancy is pricing power, not just a fuller building.

What to watch:

  • RevPOR growth outrunning expense growth per occupied room
  • RevPOR rising while occupancy (the Occupancy chart above) stalls -- a sign growth is price-only

segmentNoi.title: NOI by segment
segmentNoi.content:
Ventas runs three reporting segments: SHOP (directly-operated senior housing, the highest-growth, most operationally levered segment, ~49% of NOI), Outpatient Medical & Research (leased medical office and lab buildings, ~25%) and NNN (triple-net leased senior housing, hospitals and skilled nursing, contractual rent with little operating risk, ~25%).

For Ventas, Inc.: the mix is shifting toward SHOP as senior housing demand recovers post-pandemic; that raises both the growth rate and the cyclicality of consolidated NOI.

What to watch:

  • SHOP's share of total NOI rising (more growth, more operating risk)
  • NNN NOI holding flat to down as leases run off or get restructured

sameStoreNoiGrowth.title: Same-store NOI growth by segment
sameStoreNoiGrowth.content:
Same-store growth strips out acquisitions and disposals, isolating organic performance of properties held throughout both periods compared, by segment.

For Ventas, Inc.: SHOP same-store growth has been running well ahead of NNN's low-single-digit, contractual-escalator pace -- the gap is the senior-housing-recovery thesis in one chart; NNN is the floor, SHOP is the upside.

What to watch:

  • SHOP same-store growth decelerating toward NNN's rate (recovery maturing)
  • NNN same-store growth turning negative (tenant distress or lease restructuring)

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Ventas, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Ventas, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Ventas, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Ventas, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
